key_insight: Augmenting a 2D image-based localization database with per-image estimated depth maps enables effective geometric reasoning via dense image-to-image matching, delivering high-accuracy localization without a centralized 3D reconstruction.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between easy-to-maintain 2D image-based localization and accurate but costly-to-maintain 3D structure-based methods, enabling scalable, updatable localization with improved geometric fidelity.
method: Enrich each database image with an estimated depth map to capture local scene geometry.
Perform dense image-to-image matching between query images and depth-augmented database entries to establish robust correspondences.
Use depth-aware geometric verification and pose estimation to localize queries without building or updating a global 3D model.
impact: Offers practitioners a practical trade-off: the simplicity and updatability of image-based systems with much of the geometric accuracy of 3D pipelines, benefiting applications in robotics, AR, and large-scale mapping where frequent updates and low maintenance are essential.

paper_title: ImLoc: Revisiting Visual Localization with Image-based Representation
paper_authors: Xudong Jiang, Fangjinhua Wang, Silvano Galliani, Christoph Vogel, Marc Pollefeys
